summary: On-call kiosk login blocked by stale SSO session cookie binding after session refresh
description:
Issue summary:
When on-call engineers try to sign into the physical on-call kiosk (internal support console running in kiosk mode), SSO completes but the kiosk immediately rejects the session and shows a 403. Affected users previously had a valid session that was refreshed by the IdP due to device-attestation refresh. The kiosk appears to retain an older cookie binding value and fails authorization after the IdP refresh.

Impact:
- Multiple on-call rotations unable to access the kiosk dashboard to acknowledge alerts and run internal playbooks for ~4 hours during the window.
- Operational risk for PagerDuty handoffs where the kiosk is relied on in the NOC.

Environment:
- prod/us-east cluster behind identity-proxy v2.13.1
- Console kiosk image: redwood/console-kiosk:2026.02.12 (deployed to a pool of 6 pods)
- Okta (IdP) relevant config: device attestation refresh enabled; session rotation TTL 4h

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start with a user who has an active kiosk session (cookie present).
2) Trigger IdP session refresh/rotation (simulated by forcing device attest refresh via Okta test flow).
3) Attempt to interact with kiosk UI or re-open the console tab.
4) Kiosk reports HTTP 403 and forces a sign-out loop.

Observed logs and errors:
- identity-proxy logs: "session cookie binding mismatch: expected=sha256:abc123 got=sha256:def456"
- console auth middleware: "authorization failed: stale_bind_value"
- No application 5xxs; upstream IdP returns 200 for token exchange.

Expected behavior:
- Kiosk should accept the rotated session binding or transparently exchange/refresh the cookie binding when the IdP rotates device attest info so users are not forced out during refresh.

Workaround:
- Short-term: instruct affected engineers to perform a manual sign-in on the kiosk (clearing cookies) or use a different machine. For on-call rotations, support ran a manual cookie clear on two kiosks to restore access.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Riley Chen (reporter): Noticed multiple on-call members reporting instant sign-outs during the 05:00–07:00 window after the scheduled IdP refresh. Kiosk pods show repeated auth failures with 'stale_bind_value' message.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Support (Sofia Martinez): Temporarily advised users to clear kiosk cookies. Confirmed workaround restores access for individual test accounts. Escalating to SRE for root cause and rollback options.

2026-03-10 11:30 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally by toggling device-attestation on the IdP test tenant. Identity-proxy treats the rotated attestation as a new binding, but kiosk session binding verification is strict and rejects the rotated value. Captured proxy debug trace and token exchange trace. Linking logs: https://logs.prod.redwood/trace/4b2a8

2026-03-11 08:12 - Eng (Devon Patel): Investigating whether the binding derivation algorithm changed after the identity-proxy 2.13.1 release. Hypothesis: a change in cookie serialization ordering introduced a different hash for the same attestation set.

2026-03-12 15:40 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Verified that rolling back identity-proxy to v2.12.7 in a canary pool allowed rotated sessions to be accepted for the same test flow. Will coordinate a patch for tolerant binding check.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Devon Patel (assignee): Preparing a PR to add backward-compatible binding acceptance (allow previous bind value window of 5 minutes) and to add diagnostic metrics. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/14268
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Identity-proxy release 2.13.1 introduced deterministic field ordering when serializing the device attestation payload; this changed the input to the cookie binding hash.
- Kiosk auth middleware performs a strict equality check against a single binding value; no tolerance for rotation window.
Findings:
- Trace shows IdP rotates device attestation and issues a new claim set. Identity-proxy recalculates bind_value and issues Set-Cookie with new bind. Kiosk still presents old cookie on request causing mismatch.
- Rolling back identity-proxy to v2.12.7 suppressed the mismatch, indicating the change in proxy behavior is causal.
- No evidence of token compromise; this is an interoperability/regression issue.
Relevant links:
- Logs: https://logs.prod.redwood/trace/4b2a8
- Canary job: https://ci.redwood/job/kiosk-canary/547
- Related internal thread: slack://support/channel/oncall-kiosk-session-rotation
Next steps proposed:
- Ship a tolerant acceptance patch to kiosk auth middleware (accept last bind value for X seconds).
- Patch identity-proxy to send 'previous-bind' header during rotation as an interim compatibility signal.
- Add metric: auth.bind_mismatch.count tagged by release and region.
- Postmortem to cover rollout and test coverage gaps for cookie-binding changes.
resolution:
[Mitigation applied 2026-03-12]
- Deployed kiosk auth middleware patch that accepts the previous bind value for a 300s window while validating current bind. Deployed to canary (1 pod) then rolled to pool (6 pods) with monitoring.
- Applied a targeted rollback to identity-proxy in two affected racks while the compatibility patch rolled out.
- Created follow-up ENG task INT-212999 to harden unit/integration tests around binding serialization and to add a compatibility header for future rotations.
- Monitoring: added auth.bind_mismatch.count and alert if rate > 5/min region-wide.

Customer-facing/residual impact:
- No further kiosk outages after 2026-03-12 16:30. On-call workflows resumed. Users who were forcibly signed out had to re-authenticate once.

Follow-ups:
- ENG to release identity-proxy 2.13.2 with explicit previous-bind header and serialization test (target ship 2026-03-19).
- Postmortem doc scheduled: https://confluence.redwood/postmortems/kiosk-sso-2026-03
